questions.q: What is the very first step when adding two large numbers like 78,945 and 12,367?
questions.a: The first step is to write the numbers in columns, ensuring that the ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, and ten-thousands places are perfectly aligned. A wrong answer suggests the student treats numbers as simple strings of digits rather than placeholders of value, which leads to misalignment errors.

questions.q: When adding the ones column results in 14, what do you do with the '1'?
questions.a: You write the 4 in the ones place and "carry" the 1 over to the top of the tens column to be added with the tens digits. A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding of place value, where the student might incorrectly place the 1 in the hundreds column or ignore it entirely.

The sum is 71,110. Steps: (9+1=10; write 0, carry 1), (8+2+1=11; write 1, carry 1), (7+3+1=11; write 1, carry 1), (6+4+1=11; write 1, carry 1), (5+1+1=7). A wrong answer often indicates a failure to add the carried-over digit to the next column's total.

questions.q: If you are adding two 5-digit numbers, can the result ever be a 4-digit number? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, the sum of two 5-digit numbers will always be at least a 5-digit number (or a 6-digit number). A wrong answer shows the student does not understand that adding quantities increases the magnitude of the result.

questions.q: Is it easier to add from left to right (starting from ten-thousands) or right to left (starting from ones)? Explain.
questions.a: It is easier to add from right to left because it allows you to handle "carries" properly. If you start from the left, you would have to go back and adjust your previous digits every time a carry is generated from the column to the right, which is inefficient.

questions.q: Create an addition problem using two 5-digit numbers that requires carrying in every single column.
questions.a: An example is 55,555 + 66,666. A poor answer (e.g., 11,111 + 11,111) shows the student does not understand that carrying occurs only when the sum in a column is 10 or greater.
